core_obligations: Note that the definition of K_0(D_perf(R)) makes the map c of the preceding lemma induce a homomorphism K_0(D_perf(R)) -> K_0(R) (proof lines 36587-36590).

For a finite projective module M denote by M[0] the perfect complex with M in degree 0 and zero elsewhere, and observe that a short exact sequence 0 -> M -> M' -> M'' -> 0 of finite projective modules gives a distinguished triangle M[0] -> M'[0] -> M''[0] -> M[1] (proof lines 36593-36598).
Conclude that [M] -> [M[0]] defines a map K_0(R) -> K_0(D_perf(R)) (proof lines 36599-36600).
Observe that the composite K_0(R) -> K_0(D_perf(R)) -> K_0(R) is the identity (proof line 36603).

For the other composite, use the existence of the distinguished triangles attached to the truncations of a bounded complex M^bullet of finite projective R-modules to show that M^bullet is equivalent in K_0(D_perf(R)) to the sum of the classes of its cohomology modules placed in single degrees, so that the composite on the derived side is also the identity (proof lines 36604-36619).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the map c from the preceding card, taking a perfect complex to its alternating sum of classes in K_0(R), induces an isomorphism K_0(D_perf(R)) = K_0(R) (source lines 36579-36585). The proof builds the two inverse maps and checks both composites. It first notes that the definition of K_0(D_perf(R)) makes c induce a homomorphism K_0(D_perf(R)) -> K_0(R) (proof lines 36587-36590). For the other direction it sends a finite projective module M to the perfect complex M[0] concentrated in degree 0, and observes that a short exact sequence 0 -> M -> M' -> M'' -> 0 of finite projective modules yields a distinguished triangle M[0] -> M'[0] -> M''[0] -> M[1], so that the assignment [M] -> [M[0]] is a well-defined map K_0(R) -> K_0(D_perf(R)), the author apologising for the notation (proof lines 36593-36600). The composite K_0(R) -> K_0(D_perf(R)) -> K_0(R) is then visibly the identity (proof line 36603). The remaining direction is proved by decomposing a bounded complex of finite projective modules into the distinguished triangles supplied by its truncations (proof lines 36604-36619), which shows that the composite on the derived side is also the identity. The non-routine content is the use of the truncation triangles to promote a statement about complexes to a statement about their classes.
